title: Prior summer rain gave no clear nitrogen contrast in four British butterfly samples in 1987-2012
abstract: We tested whether prior summer rainfall slopes of butterfly site indices differed with nitrogen deposition and host-plant nitrogen. Four fixed-effect models used 352,250 records in southern England and the other British sites in 1987-1999 and 2000-2012. All four main intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Site-year, site-species and regional species-year effects controlled shared observation conditions and broad species changes. Current summer rainfall and local seasonal temperature were controls. These results do not establish that nitrogen and dry weather do not interact. Static pollution, country-average rain, selected transects, missing records and 13 year clusters per fit limit inference. The package gives frozen inputs, source hashes, code, all checks and a figure.

display.caption: Prior dry-summer slope contrasts in four British samples. Main intervals use site and year clusters and four-test correction. Sensitivity points show changes with the model or selected records. Rain and nitrogen are broad markers; the contrasts do not establish causal effects.

citations.reason: We reuse the verified site index, deposition, trait and local temperature files. This prior analysis tested temperature rather than rain. Observations overlap.
We recover three frozen raw Met Office country rainfall files from the verified bundle. We do not use its collated butterfly index.
Original biological panel and host-trait build; the immediate source preserves its derived files. We retain its build and retrieval code.
